first.text: May your umbrella turn inside out just once, on the walk that matters most.
May the remote's batteries run out at the best part of the show.
May one sock go missing from tomorrow's load.
May your shower run cold for the first ten seconds, just this once.
May the good pen be nowhere you left it, today.
May a single grain of rice find the kitchen floor.
May the last square of toilet paper be folded the wrong way.
May your coffee cool to lukewarm the moment you sit down.
May your phone buzz twice, then turn out to be nothing.
May the dishwasher leave one fork unwashed, this cycle only.
May your alarm go off one snooze earlier than planned.
May the fitted sheet slip a single corner tonight.

second.text: May the dishwasher leave exactly one fork dirty, every cycle, forever.
May one sock vanish from every load you ever run.
May your left earbud lose power first, every single time.
May the milk turn a day before the carton says it should.
May the good scissors live in a drawer you never open.
May your charger cable fray at the one spot that matters.
May the last slice always be the slightly stale one.
May the thermostat sit one degree off comfortable, permanently.
May the doorbell ring the moment you sit down to eat, every time.
May your keys hide in the coat pocket you check last.
May the WiFi drop for exactly as long as your important call.
May your umbrella turn inside out in every wind from now on.

third.text: May every pair of headphones you own tangle in your pocket, and may the knot never be the same knot twice.
May the good chair in every room you enter already be taken.
May every candle you light burn crooked down one side, forever.
May your houseplants lean toward the window with the worst view, permanently.
May the freezer frost over your favorite thing first, every time.
May the toaster favor one side, browning it dark while the other stays pale, for the rest of your days.
May every playlist you shuffle open with the same three songs.
May the parking spot nearest the door fill the instant you arrive, forever.
May your phone screen find a new smudge the second you finish cleaning it.
May the last bite of your favorite meal always slip off the fork.
May every mirror in your home be smudged in exactly the corner you always check first.
May your favorite mug grow a new hairline crack each season, and never once break cleanly.

first.text: May the printer jam on page one of your only copy.
May the meeting run five minutes long, just this once.
May your coffee go cold in the one meeting you can't leave.
May the elevator stop on every floor but yours, today.
May the good stapler be missing from your desk this morning.
May your reply-all be seen by exactly one person you'd rather it wasn't.
May the office chair squeak once, right as the room goes quiet.
May the WiFi buffer your video for three seconds during the important slide.
May the last good pen in the supply closet be gone when you get there.
May your lunch be microwaved a minute short by whoever used it before you.
May the calendar invite land during your only free hour.
May your badge fail the reader once, in front of someone.

second.text: May the printer jam on the last page of every report you submit.
May every meeting you're in run exactly nine minutes long.
May your coffee go cold before the meeting you can't leave ever ends.
May the elevator stop on every floor but yours, from now on.
May the good stapler always be missing from your desk.
May someone reply-all to the email you meant to send quietly, every time.
May the office chair squeak once per meeting, always at the wrong moment.
May the WiFi buffer for exactly three seconds during every slide that matters.
May the supply closet run out of good pens the week you need them.
May your lunch be microwaved one minute short, forever, by whoever's ahead of you.
May every calendar invite land in your only free hour.
May your badge fail the reader in front of someone, at least once a month.

third.text: May every meeting you organize run long, and may the last five minutes always be about scheduling the next one.
May your desk plant outlast everyone else's, but never quite thrive.
May the office thermostat be set by someone who is always one degree away from you, forever.
May your name be misspelled on every badge and welcome email issued to you at any job, for life.
May the good conference room always be booked exactly when you need it, and only then.
May your inbox settle at exactly one unread message you can never quite bring yourself to open.
May every group project assign you the slide nobody else wanted.
May the office coffee machine run out the moment it's your turn, forever.
May your chair's wheel catch the one loose thread in the carpet, every single day.
May your out-of-office reply always contain one small, permanent typo you never notice.
May the whiteboard marker nearest you always be the one that's nearly dry.
May every performance review mention, gently, that you could smile more.

first.text: May the light turn red the moment you approach, just this once.
May the car ahead of you brake for no reason, today.
May you catch every red light on one ordinary drive.
May the gas station nearest you be out of your grade, just once.
May someone take the parking spot you were waiting for, today.
May your GPS mispronounce one street name, badly.
May the bus pull away as you reach the stop, this one time.
May the car behind you tailgate for one uncomfortable mile.
May your windshield wipers squeak once, in traffic.
May the toll booth line you choose be the slow one, today.
May you circle the block once more than you should have to.
May the crosswalk signal count down slower than it should, just this once.

second.text: May you catch every red light on your way to anywhere that matters.
May the car ahead of you brake for no reason, on every drive.
May the gas station nearest you always be slightly more expensive than the next one.
May someone take your parking spot the moment you signal for it, forever.
May your GPS mispronounce the same street name, every time, for years.
May the bus pull away exactly as you reach the stop, from now on.
May the car behind you tailgate you for one uncomfortable mile, every drive.
May your windshield wipers squeak in every light rain.
May you always choose the slow line at the toll booth.
May the crosswalk signal always count down slower than you'd like.
May every roundabout you enter have one driver who doesn't understand roundabouts.
May your turn signal outlast every other bulb in the car, and click a half-second too slow, forever.

third.text: May every road you take home be the one under construction.
May you find the perfect parking spot, and then find it was never yours to take.
May your check-engine light come on exactly when it's least convenient, and go off again on its own, forever unexplained.
May the driver who cuts you off be, without exception, in more of a hurry than you'll ever know.
May the one pothole on your street find your tire, every winter, without fail.
May your rearview mirror slip out of place on the first turn of every drive.
May you be the car everyone lets merge, and never once say thank you for.
May the gas gauge sit on empty a little sooner than the tank actually is, for the rest of your driving days.
May every long drive end with a song stuck in your head that you didn't even like.
May the one traffic camera on your route always seem to be watching, whether it is or not.
May your car alarm go off once, for no reason, in a quiet parking lot, forever remembered by everyone nearby.
May the road home always feel one traffic light longer than it should.

first.text: May the last slice you were saving be eaten by someone else, just this once.
May a spoiler reach you before you finish the episode, today.
May someone cancel plans on you with less notice than you deserve, this one time.
May your name be left off one group photo you were actually in.
May a secret you told in confidence travel one step further than intended.
May someone borrow something of yours and return it a little worse, just once.
May your favorite seat be taken, by someone who knew it was yours.
May you be the last to hear news that concerns you directly.
May someone laugh a beat too late at your best joke, today.
May your gift be the one nobody quite remembers who gave it.
May someone take credit for one small thing you did well.
May a friend leave you on read for just long enough to notice.

second.text: May the last slice, whatever it is, always be eaten by someone else.
May spoilers reach you before you finish anything you're excited about.
May plans be cancelled on you with just enough notice to be annoying, forever.
May your name be left off group photos you were standing right next to.
May the secrets you tell always travel one step further than you meant.
May the things you lend come back a little worse, every time.
May someone always take the seat that was quietly, understood-ly, yours.
May you always be the last to hear news that concerns you.
May your best jokes land a beat late, every time, forever.
May your gifts be the ones nobody remembers giving.
May someone always take credit for the small things you did well.
May you be left on read just long enough to notice, every time.

third.text: May everyone who ever borrowed money from you forget the exact amount, forever, in their favor.
May the group chat move on to a new joke exactly as you finally understand the old one.
May the person who forwarded your private message never once feel it was a big deal.
May every reunion remind you, gently and repeatedly, of the one thing you'd rather forget.
May your most flattering photo always be the one nobody thinks to post.
May the friend who never apologizes remain, infuriatingly, easy to forgive.
May your thoughtful gifts be met with polite enthusiasm, forever, and nothing more.
May you remember everyone's birthday, and be remembered on none of yours.
May the one who wronged you go on to have, by all appearances, a very nice life.
May every story you tell be slightly better in someone else's retelling.
May you be, for the rest of your days, the reliable friend and never once the exciting one.
May the apology you're owed arrive eventually, and land just a little too late to matter.

first.text: May today contain one small inconvenience, unspecified, and thoroughly deserved.
May something minor go slightly wrong, just once, in a way you'll forget by evening.
May you drop something small and catch it, just barely, only this once.
May one text go unanswered a little longer than it should, today.
May your favorite song end just as it gets to the good part, once.
May a single cloud pass over you at the worst possible moment for a photo.
May you misplace something small, and find it an hour later, in the first place you looked.
May the elevator arrive at the exact moment you decide to take the stairs.
May a light drizzle begin the moment you step outside without an umbrella, briefly.
May your phone battery drop from 20% to 1% faster than it should, once.
May you say 'you too' when the waiter tells you to enjoy your meal, and know it, immediately.
May one page of every book you read stick slightly to the next.

second.text: May small inconveniences find you a little more often than they find anyone else.
May things go slightly wrong just often enough that you start to notice a pattern.
May you drop small things a little more than is statistically fair, and always just barely catch them.
May your favorite songs end just as they reach the good part, every time.
May a cloud pass over you at every photo that mattered.
May you misplace things a little more than you used to, and find them a little too late.
May the elevator arrive the moment you commit to the stairs, from now on.
May light rain begin the moment you leave the umbrella behind, more often than chance allows.
May your phone battery drop unreasonably fast, on the days you need it most.
May you say something slightly awkward in return to small talk, and remember it that night.
May a page in every book you own stick faintly to the next.
May your bad luck be small, constant, and impossible to complain about without sounding petty.

third.text: May you be, from this day forward, a person to whom small things simply happen — nothing dramatic, nothing worth a story, just a quiet, persistent tax on your patience.
May every queue you join move slower than the one beside it, and may the one beside it move slower the moment you switch.
May you always be one page behind in the group reading assignment, forever, gently.
May your luck be, on the whole, fine — just fine — for the rest of your natural life.
May the weather app be wrong about your day, specifically, more than anyone else's.
May you always almost win the small things — the raffle, the coin toss, the last seat.
May you be remembered as reliable, dependable, and never once as lucky.
May every shortcut you take turn out, quietly, to be the long way.
May you be, for the rest of your life, one email behind on everything that doesn't really matter.
May your name be autocorrected to someone else's, softly, forever, in ways you only half notice.
May the universe owe you nothing, and may it never once pay you back for the small, unspecified things.
May this curse itself be a little underwhelming, and may you feel, reading it, a small, petty satisfaction anyway.
